source_metadata.title: Multidose Ondansetron after Emergency Visits in Children with Gastroenteritis
authors: Pediatric Emergency Research Canada Innovative Clinical Trials Study Group

issues.description: The main article is the primary publication; appendix and protocol are supporting materials under the same publication identity and are not treated as separate studies.
The dichotomous MVS>=9 primary analysis favored ondansetron, while the continuous MVS analysis in Supplementary Table S6 had a 95% CI crossing zero. Both are preserved separately.
The intervention provided access to up to six doses, but actual multi-dose use was low; this reported exposure pattern is preserved rather than assuming scheduled multidose treatment.

extraction_limitations: Atoms remain review_status=needs_review because no human verification step was supplied in this run.
The trial protocol is lengthy; protocol-derived atoms are limited to design/amendment facts that materially affect interpretation of the reported trial.
Exploratory effect estimates are preserved as reported and tagged as exploratory; they should not be interpreted as multiplicity-controlled confirmatory findings.
The article reports that disclosure forms and a data-sharing statement are available online; those external materials were not used because this run was grounded in the provided Drive source set.
